questions.question: Jallianwala Bagh is located in which city?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amritsar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• Jallianwala Bagh is now preserved as a **national memorial**. It serves as a reminder of the sacrifices made during India’s freedom struggle.
 
• The memorial includes a **Martyrs' Well**, into which many people jumped to escape the firing, and bullet marks on the walls, which are still visible.
 
• Every year, the site is visited by tourists and locals who pay homage to the **martyrs** and reflect on India’s history of colonial resistance.

• Amritsar was founded by **Guru Ram Das**, the fourth Sikh Guru, in **1577**.
 
• The city is famous for its **Punjabi culture, cuisine**, and handicrafts.

questions.question: Children’s Day in India is celebrated to commemorate the birth anniversary of _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Children's Day** in India is celebrated annually on **14th November**. It marks the birth anniversary of **Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru**, the first Prime Minister of India.
 
• Pandit Nehru was fondly known as **Chacha Nehru** because of his deep affection for children. He believed that children were the future of the nation and emphasized their importance in building a better society.
 
• The celebration of Children's Day in India began after Nehru's demise in **1964**. Before that, Children's Day was observed in India on 20th November, which was the date recognized globally by the United Nations.
 
• Nehru was a strong advocate for the educational rights of children and played a pivotal role in establishing institutions like the **Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), and Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**.
 
• The day is celebrated across schools and educational institutions with various events like **cultural programs, competitions, and activities** that focus on the welfare and development of children.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru:**

 
 
• Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru was born on **14th November 1889** in Allahabad, India.
 
• He was a prominent leader in India's **freedom struggle** and played a key role in shaping the country's future after independence.
 
• Nehru was known for his modern outlook and vision for a technologically advanced and self-reliant India.
 
• His books like **"Discovery of India"** and **"Letters from a Father to His Daughter"** reflect his thoughts on India's heritage and his love for children.
 
 
 
• **Global Children's Day:**
 
 
• Internationally, Children's Day is celebrated on **20th November**, the date when the **United Nations General Assembly adopted the Declaration of the Rights of the Child** in 1959.
 
• The day serves as an occasion to promote the welfare and rights of children worldwide.
 
• Different countries celebrate Children's Day on various dates, but the global celebration focuses on improving the lives of children and promoting education, health, and safety.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Children's Day:**
 
 
• Children's Day aims to increase awareness about the rights, care, and education of children.
 
• It highlights the importance of creating a safe and supportive environment where children can thrive.
 
• On this day, educational institutions often organize **special programs, events, and activities** to engage children and emphasize their importance in society.
 
 
 
• **Other Important Days for Children:**
 
 
• **World Children's Day**: Celebrated globally on **20th November** to promote the welfare of children.
 
• **National Education Day**: Observed in India on **11th November** to honor the birth anniversary of **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad**, focusing on the importance of education.
 
• Various days are dedicated to children's welfare, emphasizing the need for better education, nutrition, and healthcare.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Educational Contributions:** Pandit Nehru's vision led to the establishment of several premier educational institutions in India, which continue to contribute to the nation's development.
 
• **Chacha Nehru:** His affectionate title reflects the bond he shared with children and his commitment to their welfare.
 
• **Legacy:** Nehru's ideology on children's rights and education is still relevant today, forming the foundation for various policies and schemes in India.

questions.question: Both, Rajesh Prasanna and Rishabh Prasanna are associated with which musical instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Flute**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rajesh Prasanna** and **Rishabh Prasanna** are renowned Indian musicians who are widely recognized for their exceptional skills in playing the **flute**.
 
• They both belong to the **Benares Gharana**, which is one of the oldest and most prestigious musical traditions in Indian classical music.
 
• The **flute** is a significant instrument in Indian classical music, and the Prasanna family has been associated with mastering and teaching this instrument for generations.
 
• Rajesh Prasanna and Rishabh Prasanna have gained international recognition for their mesmerizing flute performances and have represented Indian classical music on global platforms.
 
• They are known for their ability to blend traditional Indian classical music with contemporary styles, showcasing the versatility of the flute as an instrument.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Flute in Indian Classical Music:**

 
 
• The flute is one of the oldest known musical instruments and has a significant presence in Indian classical music.
 
• In Indian classical music, the bamboo flute (also called **Bansuri**) is predominantly used, which has a rich and melodious tone.
 
• The Bansuri holds a special place in Indian culture and mythology, often associated with Lord Krishna, who is depicted playing the flute in many traditional stories and art forms.
 
 
 
• **Benares Gharana:**
 
 
• The Benares Gharana is one of the most prominent musical traditions in Indian classical music, known for its focus on rhythm and melody.
 
• This Gharana has contributed significantly to the development of Indian classical music, producing numerous legendary musicians, including flutists like the Prasanna family.
 
 
 
• **Other Famous Flute Players in India:**
 
 
• **Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia:** A globally acclaimed flutist and one of the most prominent figures in Indian classical music.
 
• **Ronnie Ron:** An Indian flutist known for his work in Bollywood music.
 
 
 
• **Features of the Flute:**
 
 
• The flute is a wind instrument that produces sound from the flow of air across an opening.
 
• In Indian classical music, the Bansuri is made from bamboo and is known for its simple design and rich tonal quality.
 
• The length and diameter of the flute influence its pitch and tone.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of the Flute in Indian Mythology:**

 
 
• The flute is closely associated with **Lord Krishna**, who is often depicted playing it to create enchanting music that captivates humans and animals alike.
 
• It symbolizes love, devotion, and divine connection in Indian culture.
 
 
 
• **Global Recognition of Indian Flute Music:**
 
 
• Indian classical flute music has gained international acclaim for its soulful and meditative quality.
 
• Flute maestros like Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia have performed at prestigious global venues, spreading awareness about Indian musical traditions.

questions.question: The Aatmanirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana was implemented through which organisation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Employees Provident Fund Organisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Aatmanirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana (ABRY)** was launched as a part of the Government of India's **Aatmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan** to promote employment generation and economic recovery post the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• The scheme aims to encourage employers to create new jobs and restore employment that was impacted due to the pandemic.
 
• The **Employees Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO)**, under the Ministry of Labour and Employment, is the implementing agency for the Aatmanirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana.
 
• The government provides financial support to employers by contributing both the **employee’s share (12%)** and the **employer’s share (12%)** of contributions towards the EPF for eligible new employees.
 
• The beneficiaries of the scheme include employees who lost their jobs between **March 1, 2020, and September 30, 2020**, as well as those who were newly employed on or after October 1, 2020.
 
• The scheme covers establishments registered with the EPFO and applies to employees earning up to **Rs. 15,000 per month**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Employees Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO):**

 
 
• The EPFO is a statutory body under the administrative control of the **Ministry of Labour and Employment, Government of India**.
 
• It administers the Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF) and provides social security benefits such as **pension, insurance, and provident fund** to employees in India.
 
• It was established under the **Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952**.
 
• EPFO ensures retirement savings for employees and provides benefits like withdrawal, insurance, and pension.
 
 
 
• **Aatmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan:**
 
 
• Launched by the **Government of India** in May 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic to make India self-reliant and boost the economy.
 
• It includes measures to support **MSMEs, agriculture, healthcare, and migrant workers**.
 
• The campaign focuses on promoting local products, enhancing manufacturing capabilities, and boosting exports.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility Criteria for ABRY:**
 
 
• Employees who lost their jobs due to the pandemic from **March 1, 2020, to September 30, 2020**, and got employed on or after October 1, 2020.
 
• New employees joining the workforce between **October 1, 2020, to June 30, 2021**, earning wages less than Rs. 15,000 per month are eligible.
 
 
 
• **Benefits Under ABRY:**
 
 
• The scheme provides a **two-year EPF contribution** (12% employer + 12% employee) for establishments employing up to 1,000 workers.
 
• For establishments employing more than 1,000 workers, the government contributes only the **employee’s share** of 12% of wages.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Statistics:**

 
 
• As of **September 2021**, the scheme has provided benefits to over 15 lakh new employees and supported more than 1.2 lakh establishments.
 
• The government has allocated **Rs. 22,810 crores** for the implementation of the ABRY scheme.
 
 
 
• **Other Related Schemes:**
 
 
• **PM Garib Kalyan Yojana:** Aimed at supporting low-income groups during the COVID-19 pandemic through food grain distribution and financial assistance.
 
• **PM SVANidhi Scheme:** A micro-credit facility for street vendors affected by the pandemic, providing collateral-free loans.

questions.question: Which brick-made minaret holds the record for being the world's tallest tower at 73 meters?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Qutub Minar (India). **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tallest Brick Minaret:** Standing at approximately **73 meters**, it is the tallest brick minaret in the world.
 
• **Location & Heritage:** Situated in **Delhi, India**, and recognized as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
 
• **Architecture & Material:** Built of **red sandstone and marble**, it showcases **Indo-Islamic architecture** with intricate carvings and inscriptions.
 
• **Historical Significance:** Constructed as a **victory tower** by Qutb-ud-din Aibak in the early 13th century, symbolizing the beginning of Muslim rule in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Significance:**

 
 
• The Minaret of Jam was constructed during the rule of **Sultan Ghiyas-ud-din Ghori**, a ruler of the Ghurid dynasty.
 
• It is believed to have been built in **1190**, marking the height of the Ghurid Empire’s power and influence.
 
• The site of the minaret is associated with the ancient city of **Firozkoh**, the lost capital of the Ghurid dynasty.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Features:**
 
 
• The minaret is made entirely of **baked bricks** and is renowned for its **elaborate decorative patterns**, including Quranic inscriptions and geometric designs.
 
• Its architecture exemplifies a fusion of **Persian and Islamic styles**, reflecting the cultural and artistic exchange during the Ghurid period.
 
• The structure is divided into multiple **cylindrical tapering sections** and is supported by an octagonal base, enhancing its stability.
 
 
 
• **Preservation Challenges:**
 
 
• Due to its remote location, the Minaret of Jam has faced significant threats from **natural erosion, floods, and looting**.
 
• International efforts led by UNESCO aim to preserve the structure and mitigate risks to its stability.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Minarets:**
 
 
• **Minaret of Jam (Afghanistan):** ~65 m, historically significant, but slightly shorter than Qutub Minar.
 
• **Kalyan Minaret (Uzbekistan):** Shorter (~45 m), known for architectural beauty.
 
• **Minaret of Turin (Italy):** Modern structure (Mole Antonelliana), not a historical brick minaret.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO Designation:**
 
 
• The Minaret of Jam was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in **2002** due to its historical and architectural significance.
 
• The site is also included on the list of **World Heritage in Danger** due to ongoing threats from natural and human-induced factors.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Minaret of Jam is an **iconic representation** of Islamic art and architecture in Central Asia during the 12th century.
 
• Its **remote location** in the Ghor Province has contributed to its preservation over centuries but also poses challenges for maintenance and restoration efforts.
 
• The decoration on the minaret includes verses from the Quran, showcasing the significant role of **Islamic culture** and religion in the region during the Ghurid dynasty.
 
• Despite its historical importance, the site remains under **constant threat from environmental factors**, making its preservation a priority for international organizations.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a drawback of the barter system?

options.text: Lack of a common unit of value
Surplus goods are replaced with other goods

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Surplus goods are replaced with other goods**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lack of a common unit of value:** The barter system does not have a standard unit of value, making it challenging to determine the value of goods or services consistently. This is a major drawback of the barter system because it leads to confusion and inefficiency in transactions. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **Surplus goods are replaced with other goods:** This statement is not a drawback of the barter system. In fact, replacing surplus goods with other goods is one of the primary mechanisms of barter and is considered a benefit rather than a disadvantage. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• **Difficulty in contractual payments:** The barter system makes it difficult to handle transactions involving deferred payments or contracts, as there is no universally accepted medium of exchange. This creates inefficiencies in long-term economic arrangements. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **Double coincidence of wants:** The barter system requires that both parties have goods or services that the other desires, which is highly inconvenient and limits trade. This is one of the most significant drawbacks of the barter system. *Hence, this statement is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Barter System:**

 
 
• The barter system is one of the oldest forms of exchange, where goods and services are directly exchanged without using money.
 
• It was commonly used in ancient civilizations before the advent of currency systems.
 
• Examples include trading agricultural products for tools or livestock for textiles.
 
• The barter system works well in small, close-knit communities but becomes less practical in larger economies.
 
 
 
• **Drawbacks of the Barter System:**
 
 
• **Double coincidence of wants:** Both parties must have what the other wants, which significantly reduces the scope of transactions.
 
• **Lack of a standard unit of value:** There is no common measure to determine the worth of goods and services, leading to inefficiency.
 
• **Indivisibility of goods:** Some goods cannot be divided into smaller units for trade, e.g., livestock.
 
• **Difficulty in storing wealth:** Goods like perishable items lose value over time, making it hard to store wealth.
 
• **Deferred payments:** Future payments are difficult to manage without a universally accepted medium like money.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Money:**
 
 
• The inefficiencies of the barter system led to the development of money as a medium of exchange.
 
• Money serves as a unit of value, a store of wealth, and a medium for deferred payments.
 
• Modern economies rely on fiat currencies, digital payments, and cryptocurrencies for transactions.
 
 
 
• **Historical Example:**
 
 
• Ancient Mesopotamians used barter to exchange goods like grains, livestock, and tools.
 
• Native American tribes often traded goods like tobacco and animal pelts.
 
• Barter systems are still used in isolated or informal economies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Transition from Barter to Money:**

 
 
• The barter system laid the foundation for economic transactions, but its inefficiencies necessitated the creation of money.
 
• Precious metals like gold and silver were used initially as a medium of exchange.
 
• Later, coins and paper money became prevalent, followed by digital currencies in the modern era.
 
 
 
• **Modern Barter Systems:**
 
 
• Barter systems are still used in informal economies or during financial crises when currency loses value.
 
• Online barter platforms allow individuals to exchange goods and services without money.
 
• Examples include swapping books, clothes, or skills like graphic design for other services.
 
 
 
• **Key Economic Concept:**
 
 
• The barter system demonstrates the importance of a medium of exchange in facilitating trade and economic growth.
 
• It highlights how inefficiencies in trade can impede economic development.
 
 
 
• **Relevance Today:**
 
 
• Understanding the barter system helps in comprehending the evolution of trade and finance.
 
• It offers insights into the challenges faced by economies before the advent of monetary systems.

questions.question: Chili peppers produce a burning sensation in any tissue with which they come into contact. What is the compound responsible for this?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Capsaicin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Capsaicin** is the primary compound responsible for the burning sensation experienced when consuming chili peppers or when it comes into contact with tissue.
 
• It binds to a specific pain receptor known as **TRPV1 (Transient Receptor Potential Vanilloid 1)**, which is responsible for detecting heat and physical abrasion.
 
• The activation of TRPV1 by capsaicin tricks the brain into perceiving heat or burning, even though no actual thermal burn occurs.
 
• This compound is found in the highest concentration in the **placental tissue** of chili peppers, which surrounds the seeds.
 
• Capsaicin is insoluble in water but can be dissolved in fats and oils, making dairy products like milk effective at neutralizing its effects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Capsaicin's Uses:**

 
 
• Capsaicin is used in **topical creams and patches** to relieve pain from conditions like arthritis, muscle soreness, and nerve pain.
 
• Capsaicin is also used as an ingredient in **pepper sprays**, which are used for self-defense and crowd control.
 
• Studies suggest that capsaicin may have **metabolic benefits**, such as aiding weight loss by increasing metabolism.
 
• Capsaicin has anti-inflammatory properties and is being studied for its potential role in pain management therapies.
 
 
 
• **Other Compounds in Chili Peppers:**
 
 
• **Formic Acid:** Found in ant venom and some plants, formic acid causes irritation but is not responsible for the burning sensation of chili peppers.
 
• **Acetic Acid:** Found in vinegar, it provides a sour taste and is unrelated to the spiciness of chili peppers.
 
• **Lycopene:** A red pigment found in tomatoes and other red fruits, lycopene is an antioxidant but does not cause a burning sensation.
 
 
 
• **Scoville Heat Units (SHU):**
 
 
• The heat of chili peppers is measured in **Scoville Heat Units (SHU)**, which quantify the concentration of capsaicinoids.
 
• For example, bell peppers have 0 SHU, jalapeños range from 2,500 to 8,000 SHU, and the Carolina Reaper, one of the hottest peppers, measures over 2,200,000 SHU.
 
 
 
• **Health Benefits of Chili Peppers:**
 
 
• Chili peppers are rich in **vitamins A, C, and E**, as well as antioxidants that help combat inflammation and free radical damage.
 
• Consuming capsaicin in moderation may improve cardiovascular health and aid in digestion.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• Capsaicin does not cause tissue damage, even though it may feel like a burn; the sensation is temporary and caused by the activation of nerve receptors.
 
• Capsaicin-rich chili peppers have been used in traditional medicine for thousands of years to treat various ailments, from pain relief to digestive issues.
 
• Capsaicin has also been studied for its potential role in cancer treatment, as it may target and kill certain cancer cells without harming normal cells.

questions.question: Identify the tributary of the Brahmaputra River from the following.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Burhi Dihing**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Burhi Dihing** is a significant tributary of the Brahmaputra River, which flows through the northeastern part of India.
 
• Originating from the **Patkai Hills in Arunachal Pradesh**, Burhi Dihing flows westward and joins the Brahmaputra in Assam.
 
• The Brahmaputra River, one of India's major rivers, has several tributaries, and Burhi Dihing is among the most important ones contributing to the river's flow.
 
• Its basin supports **agriculture, biodiversity, and local communities** living along its banks in the northeastern region.
 
• The Burhi Dihing is particularly known for its contribution to the region's economic activities, such as tea cultivation and other agricultural practices.
 
• **Other tributaries** of the Brahmaputra include the Lohit, Dibang, and Subansiri rivers, which are also vital for the ecological and socio-economic landscape of the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Brahmaputra River:**

 
 
• The Brahmaputra is one of the longest rivers in the world, stretching over **2,900 km** and flowing through India, China, and Bangladesh.
 
• It originates from the **Angsi Glacier** in Tibet, where it is known as the Yarlung Tsangpo, and enters India through Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• The Brahmaputra is a lifeline for the northeastern states, supporting agriculture, transportation, and cultural practices.
 
• The river is prone to annual flooding due to heavy monsoon rains, causing displacement and damage to properties in Assam and nearby regions.
 
 
 
• **Tributaries:**
 
 
• The Brahmaputra has several tributaries, both on its northern and southern sides. Major tributaries include **Subansiri, Lohit, Dibang, Dhansiri, Burhi Dihing, and Manas.**
 
• These tributaries play a critical role in maintaining the river's flow and in supporting the biodiversity of the region.
 
• The tributaries are also significant for hydropower projects, irrigation, and transportation in the northeastern states.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Explained:**
 
 
• **Barakar:** This is a tributary of the Damodar River, located in eastern India, and does not contribute to the Brahmaputra River.
 
• **Kali Ganga:** This is not associated with the Brahmaputra River system and is typically associated with the Himalayan region's smaller rivers.
 
• **Hindan:** A tributary of the Yamuna River in northern India, Hindan is unrelated to the Brahmaputra system.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Tributaries:**
 
 
• Tributaries provide essential water resources for irrigation and drinking purposes in the northeastern region.
 
• They also contribute to maintaining the ecological balance of the Brahmaputra basin, which is rich in flora and fauna.
 
• The Brahmaputra and its tributaries are significant for cultural and religious practices in northeastern India.
 
• Many tributaries are utilized for hydropower generation, contributing to energy needs in the region.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Brahmaputra is unique among Indian rivers as it is one of the few male-named rivers, whereas most rivers in India are considered female.
 
• Its river basin supports **extensive biodiversity**, including endangered species like the Gangetic dolphin and the Bengal tiger.
 
• The Brahmaputra is a transboundary river, creating geopolitical significance for India, China, and Bangladesh.
 
• Flood management and inter-basin water sharing are critical aspects of maintaining harmony among regions benefiting from the river.

questions.question: The First Battle of Panipat (1526) marked the beginning of:

options.text: French East India Company's rule in India
British East India company's rule in India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mughal's Rule in India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **First Battle of Panipat** took place on **April 21, 1526**, between the invading forces of **Babur**, the founder of the Mughal Empire, and the army of the Delhi Sultan **Ibrahim Lodi**.
 
• This battle marked the end of the **Delhi Sultanate** and the beginning of the **Mughal Empire** in India.
 
• Babur's forces, equipped with advanced artillery and superior military tactics, decisively defeated Ibrahim Lodi's forces, despite being heavily outnumbered.
 
• The battle was significant for introducing **gunpowder and field artillery** in Indian warfare, which gave Babur a considerable advantage.
 
• After his victory, Babur established the **Mughal dynasty**, which ruled over India for more than three centuries until the advent of British colonial power.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Babur:**

 
 
• Babur was a descendant of **Tamerlane** (Timur) on his father's side and **Genghis Khan** on his mother's side.
 
• He was the ruler of the **Fergana Valley** in Central Asia before he invaded India.
 
• Babur's use of **gunpowder and artillery** in battles was revolutionary and played a crucial role in his military success.
 
 
 
• **Delhi Sultanate:**
 
 
• The Delhi Sultanate was established in the early 13th century and was ruled by several dynasties, including the Slave Dynasty, Khilji Dynasty, Tughlaq Dynasty, Sayyid Dynasty, and Lodi Dynasty.
 
• The defeat of Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat marked the end of the Sultanate.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Mughal Rule:**
 
 
• The Mughal Empire brought about significant developments in **administration, architecture, culture, and art**.
 
• Some of the notable contributions include the construction of the **Taj Mahal**, development of the **Mansabdari system**, and advancements in **literature and painting**.
 
 
 
• **First Battle of Panipat:**
 
 
• The battle was fought near the town of **Panipat**, located in present-day Haryana, India.
 
• The use of superior military technology, including **matchlock guns** and field artillery, gave Babur's forces an edge over Ibrahim Lodi's army.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **First Battle of Panipat** is one of the three major battles fought at Panipat in Indian history. The other two were the **Second Battle of Panipat** (1556) between Akbar and Hemu, and the **Third Battle of Panipat** (1761) between the Marathas and Ahmad Shah Durrani.
 
• The victory at Panipat allowed Babur to lay the foundation of the **Mughal Empire** and consolidate his power in northern India.
 
• Babur's memoir, the **Baburnama**, provides detailed accounts of his campaigns, including the First Battle of Panipat.

questions.question: How many fundamental duties were added by the 42ⁿd Constitutional Amendment Act 1976?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ten**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976**, also referred to as the "Mini Constitution," added **Ten Fundamental Duties** to the Indian Constitution under **Article 51A**.
 
• The Fundamental Duties were introduced based on the recommendations of the **Swaran Singh Committee**, which was formed in **1976**.
 
• These duties are applicable to all citizens of India and are intended to remind them of their moral obligations towards the nation.
 
• The Fundamental Duties emphasize actions like respecting the Constitution, cherishing India's heritage, and promoting harmony among all citizens.
 
• Later, in **2002**, an **11th Fundamental Duty** was added through the **86th Constitutional Amendment Act**, making the total number of Fundamental Duties **Eleven**.
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is **Ten**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Duties:**

 
 
• Fundamental Duties are enshrined in **Part IVA** of the Indian Constitution under **Article 51A**.
 
• They were inspired by the Constitution of the **former Soviet Union**.
 
• The addition of Fundamental Duties was aimed at promoting a sense of responsibility among citizens to uphold the Constitution and contribute to the nation's growth.
 
• These duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not legally enforceable, but they serve as a moral obligation for citizens.
 
 
 
• **Swaran Singh Committee:**
 
 
• This committee was constituted in **1976** by the Indian government to recommend changes to the Constitution.
 
• It suggested the inclusion of Fundamental Duties to instill a sense of duty and responsibility among citizens.
 
• Initially, the committee proposed **eight Fundamental Duties**, but ultimately **ten duties** were included in the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **List of Fundamental Duties:**
 
 
• To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions.
 
• To cherish and follow the noble ideals of freedom struggle.
 
• To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• To defend the country and render national service when required.
 
• To promote harmony and brotherhood among people transcending religious, linguistic, and regional differences.
 
• To value and preserve the rich heritage of India's composite culture.
 
• To protect and improve the natural environment.
 
• To develop scientific temper, humanism, and spirit of inquiry and reform.
 
• To safeguard public property and abjure violence.
 
• To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity.
 
 
 
• **86th Amendment (2002):**
 
 
• This amendment added the 11th Fundamental Duty, which mandates parents or guardians to provide opportunities for education to their children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• The amendment is closely linked to the insertion of **Article 21A**, which provides the Right to Education as a fundamental right.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Non-justiciable Nature:** Fundamental Duties are not enforceable by law, but they play a critical role in guiding citizens' behavior and actions.
 
• **Global Inspiration:** The concept of Fundamental Duties is inspired by the **Constitution of the USSR**, which emphasized citizens' obligations towards the state.
 
• **Legal Provisions:** Although not enforceable, the Fundamental Duties can be used by courts to interpret the scope of laws and fundamental rights.
 
• **Educational Importance:** The Fundamental Duties have been included in school curricula to inculcate civic sense and national pride among students.
 
• **First Inclusion:** The Fundamental Duties were introduced during the tenure of **Prime Minister Indira Gandhi** as part of efforts to strengthen the democratic framework of India.

questions.question: Limestone is composed of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**calcium carbonate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Limestone** is a sedimentary rock primarily composed of **calcium carbonate (CaCO₃)**, which is found in the form of the mineral calcite.
 
• It is one of the most abundant natural resources and is formed from the accumulation of the skeletal fragments of marine organisms such as coral and mollusks.
 
• The formation of limestone occurs in clear, warm, shallow marine waters. It is often deposited in layers and can be found in various geological formations.
 
• Limestone is used extensively in construction (as crushed stone for concrete and roads), manufacturing (as a raw material for cement), and as a neutralizing agent in environmental applications such as water treatment.
 
• Some varieties of limestone, such as chalk, are relatively soft, while others, like marble, which is a metamorphosed form of limestone, are much harder.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Formation of Limestone:**

 
 
• Limestone is formed through both biological and chemical processes. Biological processes involve the accumulation of shells and skeletal fragments, while chemical processes involve precipitation of calcium carbonate from water.
 
• The geological process of limestone formation can take millions of years.
 
• Regions rich in limestone deposits include the **Karst landscapes**, where limestone is eroded by water to form caves, sinkholes, and springs.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Limestone:**
 
 
• Limestone is widely used in construction as crushed stone for road building and as an aggregate in concrete production.
 
• It is the main raw material in the manufacturing of **Portland cement**, a key ingredient in concrete production.
 
• It is also used in agriculture as a soil conditioner to neutralize acidity.
 
• Limestone serves as a flux material in the production of iron and steel, helping to remove impurities.
 
• Powdered limestone is used in paints, cosmetics, and toothpaste.
 
 
 
• **Other Components of Limestone:**
 
 
• While calcium carbonate is the primary component, limestone may also contain small amounts of other minerals like quartz, feldspar, pyrite, and clay.
 
• Impurities such as iron oxide can give limestone various colors, such as red, yellow, or brown.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Limestone Formations:**
 
 
• **The Great Barrier Reef** in Australia is a massive limestone formation created by coral and marine life.
 
• Other famous limestone structures include the **White Cliffs of Dover** in England and **Carlsbad Caverns** in the United States.
 
 
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 
• **Calcium carbonate:** It is a chemical compound with the formula **CaCO₃**. It is one of the most common substances found naturally in rocks worldwide.
 
• **Sodium carbonate:** Often known as washing soda, it is not a component of limestone.
 
• **Iron oxide:** Found in minerals like hematite but is not a major constituent of limestone.
 
• **Aluminium oxide:** Found in bauxite, not limestone.

questions.question: The novel ‘Pinjar’ that was later converted into a motion picture was written by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amrita Pritam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **'Pinjar'** is one of the most renowned novels written by **Amrita Pritam**, a celebrated Indian author and poet.
 
• The novel was published in **1950** and is set during the time of the **Partition of India in 1947**.
 
• 'Pinjar' is a poignant tale that explores themes of **identity, displacement, and the plight of women** during the partition.
 
• The story revolves around the character **Puro**, a Hindu woman who is abducted by a Muslim man but later develops a complex relationship with him while dealing with the trauma of abduction and societal rejection.
 
• Amrita Pritam is regarded as one of the first prominent women Punjabi poets and authors, and she is also recognized for her contributions to Indian literature in both **Punjabi** and **Hindi**.
 
• The novel was adapted into a Bollywood movie titled **"Pinjar"** in **2003**, directed by **Chandra Prakash Dwivedi**, starring **Urmila Matondkar** and **Manoj Bajpayee**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Amrita Pritam:**

 
 
• Born on **31 August 1919** in **Gujranwala, Punjab (now in Pakistan)**.
 
• She is widely considered the **first prominent female Punjabi poet** and is often referred to as the **"Voice of Women in Punjabi Literature."**
 
• Pritam's literary contributions include over **100 books** of poetry, fiction, biographies, and essays in Punjabi and Hindi.
 
• She won the **Sahitya Akademi Award** for her work "Sunehade" in **1956** and was later honored with the prestigious **Jnanpith Award** in **1982**.
 
• Her other notable works include **'Ajj Aakhaan Waris Shah Nu'**, a poignant poem about the partition of India, and the novel **'Rasidi Ticket.'**
 
 
 
• **The Partition of India:**
 
 
• The novel 'Pinjar' is set against the backdrop of the **1947 Partition of India**, one of the most traumatic events in South Asian history.
 
• The partition led to the creation of two independent nations, **India and Pakistan**, and resulted in the **displacement of over 10 million people**.
 
• This historical event caused widespread communal violence, loss of lives, and a deep impact on the socio-cultural fabric of the region.
 
 
 
• **'Pinjar' - The Motion Picture:**
 
 
• The movie adaptation of 'Pinjar' was released in **2003** and directed by **Chandra Prakash Dwivedi**.
 
• It received critical acclaim for its portrayal of the struggles faced by women during the partition era.
 
• The film won the **National Film Award for Best Feature Film on National Integration**.
 
 
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **Krishna Sobti:** Renowned for her contributions to Hindi literature, with notable works like **'Zindaginama'**.
 
• **Ismat Chughtai:** A prominent Urdu writer, known for her progressive and feminist works like **'Lihaf'** (The Quilt).
 
• **Dharamveer Bharati:** A celebrated Hindi writer, known for his novel **'Gunahon Ka Devta'** and his work as an editor of the Hindi weekly magazine **Dharma Yug**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **'Pinjar'** highlights the **plight of women** and their struggles for survival, identity, and justice during the chaotic times of the Partition.
 
• The novel explores the themes of **gender discrimination, identity, and human resilience**.
 
• The story is considered a timeless work that sheds light on the human cost of political decisions and societal norms.
 
• Amrita Pritam's works continue to inspire readers and provide critical insights into the cultural and social history of the Indian subcontinent.

questions.question: Who among the following social reformers ruled out the practice of Sati on the basis of Hindu religious texts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raja Ram Mohan Roy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** played a crucial role in the abolition of the **Sati practice** in India. He was a prominent social reformer who used **Hindu scriptures** to argue against the practice of Sati, which involved the immolation of a widow on her husband's funeral pyre.
 
• In the early **19th century**, Raja Ram Mohan Roy actively campaigned against this inhumane tradition, emphasizing that it had no strong basis in the original Hindu scriptures. He cited texts like the **Vedas and Upanishads** to prove his point.
 
• His efforts significantly influenced the British colonial administration, leading to the promulgation of the **Bengal Sati Regulation Act in 1829**, which officially banned the practice of Sati in British India.
 
• As the founder of the **Brahmo Samaj** in 1828, Raja Ram Mohan Roy also aimed to reform Hindu society by eliminating superstitions and advocating for gender equality and rational thinking.
 
• He is often referred to as the **"Father of Modern India"** and is celebrated for his pioneering contributions to social justice and the modernization of Indian society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sati Practice:**

 
 
• Sati was an ancient Hindu funeral custom in which a widow would self-immolate on her husband's funeral pyre or be forced to do so. This practice was more prevalent in some regions of India, particularly among the upper-caste Hindus.
 
• It was based on the belief that a wife should accompany her husband even in death, often under societal pressure or coercion.
 
• The practice faced criticism from various quarters, including religious leaders, reformers, and colonial administrators, for its inhumanity and violation of individual rights.
 
 
 
• **Role of Raja Ram Mohan Roy:**
 
 
• He was born in **1772** in Bengal and was deeply influenced by the principles of social reform and rational thinking.
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy used his deep knowledge of Sanskrit and Hindu scriptures to challenge orthodox practices that were not supported by religious texts.
 
• He founded the **Brahmo Samaj**, an influential socio-religious reform movement aimed at combating social evils like caste discrimination, polygamy, and child marriage.
 
 
 
• **Bengal Sati Regulation Act, 1829:**
 
 
• This act was passed by **Lord William Bentinck**, the then Governor-General of India, to officially abolish the practice of Sati.
 
• The law declared Sati illegal and punishable by criminal courts as culpable homicide.
 
• The regulation was a landmark move in the history of social reforms in India and set the stage for further efforts to improve the status of women in society.
 
 
 
• **Other Reformers:**
 
 
• **Jyotiba Phule**: Known for his efforts in promoting education among women and the lower castes. He did not directly work to abolish Sati.
 
• **Swami Vivekananda**: Focused on spiritual awakening and the revival of Hinduism but did not address Sati.
 
• **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar**: Played a significant role in widow remarriage and women's education but was not involved in the abolition of Sati.

questions.question: Which of the following classical dance styles manifests the element of sky?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathakali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kathakali** is a classical dance-drama of Kerala, India, known for its elaborate costumes, intricate makeup, and storytelling through gestures, expressions, and movements.
 
• The dance form integrates elements of nature, including **sky, earth, water, fire, and air**, into its performances, symbolically representing the universe.
 
• The element of the **sky** in Kathakali is manifested through expansive hand gestures, eye movements, and the portrayal of celestial characters such as gods or divine beings.
 
• Performers use their expressions and movements to depict various cosmic elements and celestial realms, making Kathakali a reflection of the universe.
 
• This dance form is deeply rooted in Hindu mythology and Sanskrit literature, often narrating stories from the **Ramayana, Mahabharata, and Puranas**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manipuri:**

 
 
• Manipuri is a classical dance form originating from **Manipur**, India.
 
• It emphasizes graceful movements and devotional themes, often focusing on the **Vaishnavite tradition**.
 
• This dance form does not specifically emphasize the element of the sky.
 
 
 
• **Kathak:**
 
 
• Kathak originates from **North India** and is characterized by intricate footwork and spins.
 
• It primarily revolves around storytelling and rhythmic patterns rather than representing cosmic elements like the sky.
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi:**
 
 
• Kuchipudi is a dance form from **Andhra Pradesh**, blending classical dance and drama.
 
• Although it incorporates narratives and expressions, it does not specifically manifest the element of the sky.
 
 
 
• **Important Characteristics of Kathakali:**
 
 
• Kathakali performers undergo rigorous training to master facial expressions, gestures, and body movements.
 
• It uses elaborate costumes, including large headgear, painted faces, and colorful attire, symbolizing various characters.
 
• Music in Kathakali includes traditional instruments like **chenda, maddalam, and cymbals**.
 
• Kathakali is traditionally performed during the night, lasting up to several hours, and often accompanied by Sanskrit or Malayalam verses.

questions.question: Which of the following amendments, made in September 2023, is known as 'Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**106th Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**​106th Constitutional Amendment Act – Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (September 2023):**

__
 
• **Enactment & Provision:** Introduced as the **128th Constitutional Amendment Bill** in September 2023; became the **106th Amendment Act**. Mandates **33% reservation for women** in **Lok Sabha, State Assemblies, and Delhi Legislative Assembly**.
 
• **Intersectionality:** **One-third of SC/ST reserved seats** are further reserved for **women of those categories**.
 
• **Sunset Clause:** Reservation initially valid for **15 years**, extendable by a **law passed by Parliament**.
 
• **Implementation Timeline:** Will come into effect **after the first delimitation exercise** following the **first census after commencement**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Context:**

 
 
• The discussion around **women's reservation in politics** began in the **1990s**, but it took decades for significant progress to be made.
 
• Women's representation in Indian legislatures has historically been low, with less than **15%** representation in the Lok Sabha before this amendment.
 
• Several states in India already have **33% to 50% reservation** for women in local bodies, such as Panchayati Raj Institutions.
 
 
 
• **Implementation:**
 
 
• The **128th Amendment** ensures that one-third of the seats in the **Lok Sabha** and **state assemblies** are reserved for women.
 
• The reserved seats will be rotated periodically to cover all constituencies over time.
 
• The implementation is contingent upon the completion of delimitation exercises based on the **2021 Census**.
 
 
 
• **Impact:**
 
 
• This amendment is expected to lead to a significant increase in the number of women in legislative bodies, paving the way for better representation of their concerns and issues.
 
• Enhanced representation is likely to result in improved policymaking on issues such as **women's health, education, employment, and safety**.
 
• It is also anticipated to inspire more women to participate in politics and public life.
 
 
 
• **International Context:**
 
 
• Many countries, such as **Rwanda**, **Sweden**, and **Norway**, have achieved high levels of women’s representation in politics through similar measures.
 
• The global average of women in national parliaments is approximately **26.4%**, highlighting the need for India to catch up in terms of gender parity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• The **73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments** (1992) reserved **33% of seats for women** in Panchayati Raj Institutions and Urban Local Bodies.
 
• The **Article 243D** of the Indian Constitution ensures reservation for women in Panchayats.
 
 
 
• **Global Perspective:**
 
 
• Countries like **Rwanda** have achieved over **60% representation** of women in Parliament, showcasing the success of reservation policies.
 
• India’s move aligns with global trends towards improving gender balance in political representation.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Implementation:**
 
 
• Ensuring effective implementation of the reservation policy across all states and constituencies may pose logistical challenges.
 
• Delimitation exercises based on the **2021 Census** are necessary for the amendment to be fully operational.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India describes a key feature of 'Universal Adult Franchise' that grants the right to vote to citizens, above the age of 18 years in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 326**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 326** of the **Indian Constitution** deals with **Universal Adult Franchise** and grants the **right to vote** to citizens of India who are above the age of **18 years**.
 
• This article ensures that elections to the House of the People and Legislative Assemblies are conducted on the basis of adult suffrage.
 
• Under this provision, every citizen of India who is above 18 years of age and is not disqualified due to reasons such as non-residence, unsoundness of mind, or criminal conviction has the right to vote. 
 
• The **minimum voting age** was earlier **21 years** but was reduced to **18 years** by the **61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988**.
 
• By upholding the principle of adult suffrage, Article 326 aims at fostering **democratic participation** among citizens, ensuring equal opportunity to influence governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Universal Adult Franchise:**

 
 
• The concept of **Universal Adult Franchise** is a fundamental feature of democracy that ensures **equality in participation** irrespective of caste, creed, religion, gender, or financial status.
 
• The principle is widely adopted in democratic countries across the globe, including India, and serves as the foundation for conducting free and fair elections.
 
• The **61st Constitutional Amendment Act** reduced the voting age from **21 years** to **18 years**, enabling greater participation of youth in the democratic process.
 
 
 
• **Other Related Articles in the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• **Article 324:** Deals with the establishment and powers of the **Election Commission of India** to conduct free and fair elections.
 
• **Article 325:** Prohibits discrimination based on religion, race, caste, or sex in voter registration.
 
• **Article 327:** Empowers Parliament to make laws regarding elections to legislatures.
 
 
 
• **Global Perspective:**
 
 
• Countries like the **United States**, **United Kingdom**, and **Australia** also follow the principle of Universal Adult Franchise, although the minimum voting age may vary.
 
• Globally, many nations use Universal Adult Franchise as a benchmark to ensure **equal political rights** for all citizens.
 
 
 
• **Important Amendments:**
 
 
• **61st Constitutional Amendment (1988):** Reduced the voting age from **21** to **18** years in India.
 
• This amendment was introduced to enhance youth participation in shaping the nation's democratic process.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of Universal Adult Franchise:**

 
 
• Provides **equal voting rights** to all citizens above the age of 18 years irrespective of social or economic status.
 
• Strengthens the democratic process by ensuring wide-scale participation across diverse sections of society.
 
• Serves as a tool for citizens to exercise their **right to influence governance** and policymaking.
 
 
 
• **Role of Election Commission:**
 
 
• The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** is the constitutional authority responsible for conducting elections in a free, fair, and impartial manner.
 
• ECI ensures that every eligible voter can exercise their right to vote without any discrimination or obstacles.
